title: trader-advisor — an advisor that earns the right to speak (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: It ships one seed exam — 10 costs-and-constraints questions and an llm_judge rubric — and zero track record. The paper broker's journal writes that second dataset.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the keys
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — Anthropic, a Thredz wiki key, and a search provider.

verify.note: operator-supplied demos/.env; this starter needs THREDZ_API_KEY as well as a model key

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec — an advisor that starts with nothing

beats.label: The header: three pieces do the work
beats.cue: A hosted brain, the study discipline, and a referee. And it cannot execute a real trade.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: target: cli — the interactive advisor. The always-on one is a second file, same brain.

beats.label: Give it a hosted brain
beats.cue: Wiki articles hold the playbooks; goals are the metric ticks the dashboard charts.

beats.label: Point the learning discipline at trading
beats.cue: A domain, a curriculum file, an allowlist of sources, and an exam it has to sit.

beats.label: Open the learning ladder
beats.cue: Tier 1 is the cost stack, because it gates everything. /reflect edits this file.

beats.label: Pick the model, and a fallback
beats.cue: “long study passes survive a provider hiccup” — the fallback is a spec field.

beats.label: Write the discipline down
beats.cue: “Costs first. Process over outcome. The broker is the referee. Trade only written playbooks.”

beats.label: Add the read-only researcher
beats.cue: One narrow question, primary sources, 2–4 verbatim cited snippets, 180 words, no synthesis.

beats.label: Eight tools, plus the paper brokerage
beats.cue: A zero-dependency stdio MCP server in this repo; its tools arrive as broker__*.

beats.label: Open the referee
beats.cue: Real fees, settled cash, market hours, the risk rail, the confidence gate — enforced in code.

beats.label: Wire ratings into the flywheel
beats.cue: Stars on its answers distil into a versioned trader-advisor-ratings dataset — once five unprocessed ratings have piled up, at a `crewhaus run` teardown.

beats.label: Make research friction-free
beats.cue: mode: default, and reading, searching and fetching never stop to ask.

beats.label: Let it write to its own brain
beats.cue: “The wiki is the job” — plus the goal ticks the Thredz dashboard cards read.

beats.label: Let it trade — on paper
beats.cue: Free to act, because the broker enforces the rails and no tool here touches real money.

beats.label: Let it curate its own exam
beats.cue: It may edit the curriculum and the eval assets. Markdown and JSONL only — nothing else.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the tool-scope audit.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees.” Too long for a terminal — send it to the scratch dir.

verify.note: the whole lowered IR, redirected so the next beat can open it (a pipe into head would swallow the exit code)

beats.label: Read the IR
beats.cue: Both MCP servers, lowered: the local broker on bun, and thredz as npx thredz-mcp with its env refs typed.

beats.label: Project it as an agent loop
beats.cue: Perceive, act, evaluate against its own exam, update the wiki — and what it still lacks.

verify.note: read-only loop projection; warns that no budget: is set

beats.label: Compile the bundle
beats.cue: No key, no network: one YAML in, a Bun program you own out.

verify.note: emits agent.ts + a generated README and registers the spec version

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: Every permission rule and both MCP servers, compiled into one file.

beats.label: Check the bundle for real — and meet the gate
beats.cue: Assertion ok, install ok — then the boot halts on THREDZ_API_KEY. Exit 21, by name. --check scrubs the environment, so exporting the key changes nothing: the gate is structural.

verify.note: deliberate RED (exit 1): assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot exits 21 because the synthesized thredz MCP server declares a required THREDZ_API_KEY. Measured both ways — with the key exported the output is byte-identical, because --check boots with a scrubbed env and an empty --env-file. No env scrub needed here to be deterministic.

beats.label: Boot the referee on its own
beats.cue: Before the model: the broker is a zero-dependency stdio program. One JSON-RPC line in — buy 50 AAPL, no stop.
beats.command: echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"paper_buy","arguments":{"symbol":"AAPL","qty":50,"playbook":"breakout-pullback","thesis":"Base breakout on volume; exit back inside the base."}}}' | bun mcp/paper-broker.ts > live/broker.jsonl

verify.note: no key, no network: paper_buy validates thesis/playbook/stop before it ever fetches a quote, and a rejected order writes no ledger state. The boot banner (mode=paper seed=$5000) prints on stderr, the reply lands in live/broker.jsonl.

beats.label: Read the verdict
beats.cue: “REJECTED: a stop price is required. No stop, no trade — the risk rail needs the R denominator.” Enforced in code, not asked of the prompt.

beats.label: Launch the advisor
beats.cue: [needs-key] target cli, so run compiles in memory and drops straight into the REPL.

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs Anthropic + Thredz credentials

beats.label: Ask what a round trip costs
beats.cue: [needs-key] The starter's own opening question — costs first, before any idea.
beats.text: What would a round trip on 50 shares of AAPL actually cost me?

beats.label: Send it to study
beats.cue: [needs-key] Logged knowledge gaps first, then the next unchecked rung on the ladder.

beats.label: Sit the exam
beats.cue: [needs-key] The costs-and-constraints exam. Every failed question auto-logs as a gap.

beats.label: Scan the watchlist
beats.cue: [needs-key] No written playbook, no trade — and the broker rejects anything without a stop.
beats.text: Scan SPY, AAPL, BTC-USD and paper trade any playbook that triggers.

beats.label: Ask for the scorecard
beats.cue: [needs-key] Cold start is honest: the report says the confidence gate is far from passing.
beats.text: Show the journal and the performance report.

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.

groups.title: One more thing · the same advisor, always on

beats.label: Open the daemon spec
beats.cue: Same brain, target: channel — a 6h study heartbeat and a market-hours scan cron.

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: One spec, four programs: the daemon, the gateway, the session router, and the agent. --check asserts the shape, installs the deps and boots it: GREEN, no key in the room.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated (reached its spec env refs gate). --check is also what writes the bundle's pinned package.json and installs into it; a plain `compile -o` emits source files only, so `bun install --cwd live/daemon` there would install the enclosing repo instead.

beats.label: Open the bundle's manifest
beats.cue: An ordinary Bun package — every dependency is an @crewhaus/* pinned to this CLI's version, and nothing else.

beats.label: Ask what it still needs
beats.cue: Named, actionable, exit 1 — every missing Slack credential, before the daemon dies at boot.
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET crewhaus channel verify daemon.yaml

verify.note: deliberate non-zero: both checks fail by name, exit 1. The `env -u` is load-bearing — Setup already sourced demos/.env into this same terminal, and with SLACK_* set this command calls slack.com auth.test live and its exit code depends on whether the token is real.

beats.label: Boot the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] Run it from inside this directory — the broker is wired by a relative path.

verify.note: needs SLACK_* + THREDZ_API_KEY and a public URL for /slack/events; `crewhaus channel provision daemon.yaml --base-url <public-url>` wires the Slack app

beats.label: Open the numbers it starts from
beats.cue: A hand-checked 2026 cost table with effective dates — the seed the broker's defaults mirror.
